transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jesse Patel, Lina Gomez, Marcus Li (Redwood) — Arianna Cole, Devon Morris, Samir Chaudhry, Priya Nair (Emberfield)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Kickoff for Redwood hosted + private hybrid deployment for Emberfield. Primary objectives: reduce inference latency for product search assistant, ensure data residency and auditability, define network topology for VPC/private endpoint.
- Security review items captured (SOC2, KMS, audit logs).
- Next steps: onboarding runbook, VPC walkthrough, initial pilot timeline (2–3 weeks to pilot).

Topics covered: onboarding plan, network/VPC, dedicated vs hosted, SSO/KMS, pilot success criteria, timeline, stakeholder roles

Links referenced: onboarding runbook (placeholder) https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/emberfield-onboard, discovery deck https://redwood.example.com/decks/emberfield-kickoff.pdf, security pack https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-2024.pdf

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jesse from Redwood, I'm the AE, with Lina and Marcus. How's everyone doing over there?
[00:14] Arianna: Good yep thanks, Arianna here, excited to kick this off. We have a few people on from platform and security as well.
[00:21] Devon: Hi all, Devon. We'll jump into networking details later.
[00:27] Jesse: Great, so goal for today is to align on onboarding steps, security asks, and nail down dates for the pilot. Lina, do you want to run through the high-level plan?
[00:35] Lina: Sure — quick high level. We usually do a two week sprint for initial pilot: day 0–2 network and creds, day 3–7 deploy model + smoke tests, week two integrate calls and run latency loads. We'll hand off runbooks, and Marcus will do the VPC walkthrough.
[00:48] Marcus: Yep, I'll also show the KV-cache warmup patterns and batching config we recommend for search workloads.
[00:56] Priya: Quick Q — are you recommending hosted or dedicated to start? We heard both options in the deck.
[01:03] Jesse: Good question. For the search assistant, if your concurrency is modest we can start on hosted with private endpoints; if you need predictable p99 latencies under heavy concurrency, Dedicated reserved GPUs would be better. There's a tradeoff cost vs latency.
[01:20] Samir: From security's side we care about audit logs and key control — we need to see KMS integration and that audit trails are customer-accessible. Also data retention settings.
[01:32] Lina: Yes that's in the security pack we shared; we can walk through KMS options: Redwood-managed or customer-managed with HSM via KMS. Marcus, can you speak to how logs are surfaced?
[01:44] Marcus: Sure — we push structured traces to your SIEM via an outbound connector, and we surface per-token cost and latency breakdown in the console. There is an option to stream full audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket. There may be some names in the export that are a bit off, sorry the exporter sometimes garbles proper nouns.
[02:05] Devon: About the VPC peering — we need private endpoints, not full peering, because our infra team won't allow cross-account peering. Can you support private endpoint + NAT egress to monitoring?
[02:18] Marcus: Yes, private endpoint plus egress is supported. We'll provide a step-by-step peering/endpoint diagram. I'll mark the egress IP ranges you'll need to whitelist.
[02:29] Arianna: Timeline expectations — how long before we can run a pilot?
[02:35] Lina: If network and creds are ready within a week, pilot deploy and basic validation can be 10 business days. So target pilot start around 2025-09-17 if we hit those network dates.
[02:47] Priya: That seems reasonable, we have a change freeze window 9/11–9/14 but can do prework.
[02:55] Samir: On compliance, we'll want to review SOC2 artifacts. Do you have SOC2 type 2?
[03:03] Jesse: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO documents — link in the chat. I'll ask Lina to re-share the latest package.
[03:11] Lina: I'll share, and also include our data handling FAQ — note sometimes the doc filenames are weird on export.
[03:18] Devon: One technical ask — we want to quantify cost: can you show per-token unit economics for embeddings + generation?
[03:26] Marcus: We have a cost calculator and we'll run your sample traces offline to estimate. For the pilot, we can use a mid-sized quantized model to keep tokens costs lower.
[03:37] Arianna: Who on your side will be our main contact during the pilot?
[03:41] Jesse: Lina is the CSM lead, Marcus is the SE for technical work. I'll be the commercial owner.
[03:47] Marcus: Also for the VPC walkthrough I'll schedule a 45 minute deep-dive with Devon and Priya.
[03:54] Priya: Please include a runbook that shows how to rotate keys and revoke tokens.
[03:59] Marcus: Yep, rotation and RBAC actions are documented. There's a small gap in the UI for bulk revocations, we can script it for you.
[04:08] Samir: Can you confirm where KV cache sits — does any customer data persist on Redwood-managed GPUs?
[04:16] Marcus: Good point. The KV cache is ephemeral in memory tied to the instance; we don't persist customer prompts to disk unless you enable logging. Persistent caches are optional and can be in your VPC if you want.
[04:29] Devon: Networking — we'll send a list of restricted subnets, and we need the list of egress IPs.
[04:36] Marcus: Will do — egress list and endpoints doc by Friday.
[04:41] Arianna: Objection earlier from our procurement — they asked about dedicated contract minimums. What are typical committed capacities?
[04:49] Jesse: Dedicated typically starts at a monthly commit for a GPU pool; we can propose a 3-month pilot discounted rate. I'll send an estimate.
[04:58] Priya: Any pitfalls you see for on-prem connectivity? We're not fully air-gapped but some data paths are limited.
[05:05] Lina: For on-prem or air-gapped, we do a private deployment package — that needs more lead time and an ops ticket. For most customers, private endpoint + VPC is enough.
[05:16] Devon: For the pilot we'll stay in private endpoint mode. If successful we'll scope a Dedicated pool later.
[05:22] Jesse: Great. Quick walkthrough of the onboarding checklist — I'll read out items and we can call out owners.
[05:27] Jesse: 1) NDA/contract signed (Jesse) — status?
[05:31] Arianna: Legal is finalizing, expect signed by 9/9.
[05:34] Jesse: 2) Network details and CIDR (Devon) — due 9/9.
[05:38] Devon: noted.
[05:39] Jesse: 3) IAM/SAML details for SSO (Arianna) — due 9/10.
[05:43] Arianna: We'll share SSO metadata.
[05:45] Jesse: 4) Initial sample data and traces (Emberfield) — for cost sim and quality checks.
[05:50] Arianna: We'll provide a small set of production-like traces.
[05:53] Lina: 5) Security review (Samir) — I'll schedule a call to go line-by-line if needed.
[05:58] Samir: Yes please, we'll likely have follow-up questions around encryption at rest for logs.
[06:04] Marcus: To be clear — logs can be stored in your bucket encrypted under your KMS key; Redwood will not hold that key unless you opt in.
[06:14] Priya: Regarding monitoring — can we export prom-style metrics?
[06:18] Marcus: Yes, metrics export via Prometheus-compatible endpoint or push to your monitoring. We'll add a sample config.
[06:25] Arianna: Any change windows or service interruptions to be aware of during pilot?
[06:30] Jesse: For hosted pilots, we manage rolling updates — minimal interruptions. If you opt for Private on-prem, patches require maintenance windows.
[06:40] Devon: Let's talk about success criteria — what would you propose as pilot KPIs?
[06:45] Lina: I'd propose: p99 latency < 300ms on 95% of samples, accuracy/quality metrics above baseline from your current model, and error rate < 0.5% under normal load. Those are adjustable.
[06:56] Arianna: That p99 seems aggressive; can we set a soft target and then a hard SLA for Dedicated if needed?
[07:03] Jesse: Absolutely — we'll run the pilot to validate and then discuss dedicated SLAs if you need guaranteed p99.
[07:11] Samir: A couple of notes — we'll need an inventory of subprocessors and data flow diagrams for our audit.
[07:18] Lina: We'll supply a subprocessors list and data flow. I'll add it to the runbook.
[07:23] Arianna: Great. Can you also share a troubleshooting playbook for common errors?
[07:27] Marcus: Yep, include steps for degraded latency, cache warming, and model fallback policies.
[07:32] Devon: On fallback — if primary model is unavailable do you have automatic fallback to a quantized variant?
[07:36] Marcus: We support fallback chains; we can set that policy per-route. There are cost/latency tradeoffs but it's a straightforward config.
[07:44] Priya: One more security question — do you support customer-managed HSM for keys?
[07:48] Jesse: Yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments and for certain Dedicated options.
[07:55] Samir: For the audit we want to see sample logs for a week of requests — is that possible?
[07:59] Lina: We can provide sanitized examples and an export of the schema.
[08:04] Arianna: OK — I think we have alignment on major items. Let's capture next steps.
[08:09] Jesse: I'll summarize — Lina will send runbook + security pack by 2025-09-08. Marcus and Devon to set VPC walkthrough 45m by 2025-09-10. Emberfield to send CIDR + sample traces by 2025-09-09. Samir to send any outstanding compliance questions by 2025-09-12.
[08:29] Devon: Sounds good.
[08:31] Arianna: Thanks all.
[08:33] Jesse: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[08:36] (End of recorded segment)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mislabels (Speaker names sometimes generic), minor transcription errors where product names like "KV cache" might become "K V cash" or model names garbled. There is natural speech, interruptions, and occasional filler words.
